title: Running through August 30th at the Cherry Lane Theatre in NYC #theatr...
transcript: They have so much raw chemistry, but they're both resistant to intimacy and vulnerability. So you get a tale as old as time: the “will they, won't they” romance. Shifters is a critically acclaimed play from London by Benedict Lombe that tells this non linear story flashing back and forth between different eras of a romantically charged friendship. It took me a little while to get into the play, especially as the first part is a lot more narration heavy than I usually like. But as we spend more time with them, it's really tough not to get invested in their relationship and feel deeply for them as you watch them in this push and pull game, both with each other and themselves. And while the romance is the main focus of the narrative, Lombe also thoughtfully uses their African heritage, (his Nigerian and her Congolese) to inform their experiences. In particular, as they both deal with loss in their own ways, their memories of their culture, from the music to the food, kind of help them find solid footing in their lives that keep shifting. And all of that was heightened significantly by the charismatic and emotionally rich performances from Daniel Ezra and Heather Agyepong. As we jump back and forth between the different eras in their relationship, I did sometimes struggle to keep track of which one we were in. Even though they use lighting cues to help us out, I still sometimes got a little lost. But I did like the fact that it was non linear. Sometimes with these “will they, won't they” stories, it feels like we're just running out the clock until they inevitably make up their minds. But here it feels like we're filling in the gaps of a composite portrait that informs where they are now and what exactly has kept them apart.
reasoning: Reviewer praises the performances, non-linear structure, and emotional investment, but notes caveats about narration-heavy opening and difficulty tracking timelines. Overall a clear recommendation with reservations.
